stances.claim: On the crest of expected Philippine arbitration victory, CJ agrees with President Duterte that 'we must not taunt or flaunt our triumph' -- because the PH and China enjoy a long history of friendship and excellent diplomatic/political/trade relations, this dispute is only one aspect of a broader long relationship, and humility is the better course for continued engagement; bilateral negotiation should not be ruled out after victory, since China has always wanted it.

The Tribunal's earlier 151-page Award (Oct 29, 2015) already settled China's jurisdiction objection -- finding jurisdiction notwithstanding China's absence or default -- and the Tribunal's procedural conduct (copying China with all communications, giving notice, granting response time, remaining open to participation at any stage) was procedurally scrupulous, making the impending Tuesday merits decision legitimately binding.
stances.rhetorical_move: procedural-legitimacy framing (Tribunal's scrupulous conduct overrides absent-party objections)

stances.claim: Grouping the PH's 15 submissions into three basic claims yields: (1) nine-dash-line invalidity + Unclos-governance of SCS rights; (2) feature-classification doctrine (islands generate EEZ/continental shelf, rocks generate 12-NM territorial sea, low-tide elevations and submerged banks generate nothing, no reclamation alters status); (3) China's violation of PH sovereign rights via interference + environmentally harmful construction/fishing -- and each grant carries distinct strategic benefits (freedom of navigation, free EEZ exploitation, end to Chinese chasing of PH fishermen and reef destruction).

The Itu Aba complication -- ~0.5 sq km (46 hectares), ~200 NM off Palawan, Taiwanese-occupied -- is the most consequential variable: if ruled an 'island,' it could generate a huge EEZ extending close to Palawan, and because PH recognizes only one China, the Taiwanese occupation is deemed Chinese, meaning China could exploit that EEZ with naval protection.

Critically, the PH did not ask for and the Tribunal will not grant any sovereign or ownership rights over any land mass -- the Tribunal's jurisdiction is limited only to maritime rights under UNCLOS; this is a crucial scope-limit that the public should understand so the victory's nature is not misrepresented.
stances.rhetorical_move: scope-limit clarification (maritime rights only, not sovereignty over land)

notable_anecdotes: The 'taunt or flaunt' alliteration borrowed from Duterte and endorsed by CJ -- a memorable phrase pairing that captures the humility-in-victory thesis in three syllables.

The Tribunal's procedural scrupulousness despite China's absence: 'it would copy China with all communications, arguments and documents in the case, give it notice of all hearings, grant it adequate time to respond' -- a four-step due-process catalog showing the Tribunal went above and beyond.

The Itu Aba precise specifications: 'about one-half square kilometer (about 46 hectares) of soil formation lying a little over 200 nautical miles off the coast of Palawan and occupied by Taiwanese soldiers' -- quantified geography demonstrating the scale of the potential EEZ-overlap problem.

The one-China-policy logical chain: 'Since we recognize only one China, then the Taiwanese occupation is deemed to be that of China. Despite its small size, Itu Aba could generate a huge EEZ extending very close to Palawan, an EEZ that China could exploit with the protection of its navy' -- a tight three-sentence consequence chain.

The scope-limit closing sentence: 'Note that the Philippines did not ask for, and the Tribunal will not grant, any sovereign or ownership rights over any land mass. Reason: The Tribunal's jurisdiction is limited only to maritime rights recognized under the Unclos.' -- using 'Note' as instructional-attention marker and the explicit 'Reason' format characteristic of CJ pedagogy.

The bilateral-negotiation overture: 'We should not, after our victory, rule out bilateral negotiation, as China has always wanted' -- anticipating diplomatic flexibility before the verdict is even rendered.

one_paragraph_summary: Panganiban writes on the crest of an expected Philippine arbitration victory, agreeing with President Duterte that 'we must not taunt or flaunt our triumph.' The Philippines and China enjoy a long history of friendship and excellent diplomatic, political, and trade relations -- this dispute is only one aspect of that broader relationship -- and humility in victory is the better course for continued friendly engagement; the PH should not, after victory, rule out bilateral negotiation, which China has always wanted. China opted not to participate, and the PH was allowed to present ex parte. Through diplomatic Notes Verbale, position papers, media announcements, and letters to Tribunal members, China repeatedly argued the Tribunal had no jurisdiction. The earlier 151-page Award (Oct 29, 2015) already upheld jurisdiction notwithstanding China's absence -- and the Tribunal announced it would issue its merits decision the impending Tuesday. Despite China's absence, the Tribunal procedurally copied China with all communications, gave notice of all hearings, granted adequate response time, and remained open to China's participation at any stage. The PH's Memorial prayed for 15 submissions, which CJ's earlier column (11/8/15) grouped into three basic claims. First, declarations that the parties' SCS rights and obligations are governed by Unclos and that China's nine-dash-line historic-rights claims are inconsistent with the Convention and invalid; a grant invalidates the nine-dash line and opens freedom of navigation for the US, Australia, Japan, and other big powers. Second, determination of feature characterization (islands generate EEZ + continental shelf up to 200 NM; rocks generate 12-NM territorial sea; low-tide elevations and submerged banks generate nothing; no amount of artificial reclamation alters status); a grant means PH can freely explore/develop/extract/utilize EEZ resources particularly oil and gas, legally barring China -- though the Itu Aba complication (about 0.5 sq km / 46 hectares, ~200 NM off Palawan, Taiwanese-occupied) looms: if ruled an 'island,' it could generate a huge EEZ close to Palawan, and since PH recognizes only one China, the Taiwanese occupation is deemed Chinese, meaning China could exploit that EEZ with naval protection. Third, declarations that China has violated the Convention via interference with PH sovereign rights and through constructions and fishing harming the marine environment; a grant means China can no longer legally chase PH fishermen or ruin EEZ reefs and ecology. The PH did not ask for, and the Tribunal will not grant, any sovereign or ownership rights over any land mass -- the Tribunal's jurisdiction is limited only to maritime rights under Unclos.
